questions.q: Explain how the definite integral $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ is defined as a limit of Riemann sums, and write the limit expression using sigma notation.
questions.target: Sums as limits: the definite integral
questions.answer: $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(x_i^*)\Delta x$, where $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and $x_i^*$ is any sample point in the $i$-th subinterval — as $n\rightarrow\infty$ (subintervals shrink to zero width), all Riemann sum types (left, right, midpoint) converge to the same value, the exact signed area under $f$.
questions.explanation: $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(x_i^*)\Delta x$, where $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and $x_i^*$ is any sample point in the $i$-th subinterval — as $n\rightarrow\infty$ (subintervals shrink to zero width), all Riemann sum types (left, right, midpoint) converge to the same value, the exact signed area under $f$.

questions.q: Determine whether the Left Riemann Sum overestimates or underestimates $\int_0^4 x^2\,dx$, and explain why using the shape of the graph.
questions.target: Sums as limits: the definite integral
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, the left endpoint of each subinterval gives the smallest function value on that subinterval, so the Left Riemann Sum UNDERESTIMATES the true area (confirmed: $L_4=14 < \frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$).
questions.explanation: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, the left endpoint of each subinterval gives the smallest function value on that subinterval, so the Left Riemann Sum UNDERESTIMATES the true area (confirmed: $L_4=14 < \frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$).

questions.q: The graph shows $f(x)=x^2$ on $[0,4]$. Use the graph to explain why the Right Riemann Sum $R_4=30$ (found earlier) overestimates the true area, and why the Left Riemann Sum $L_4=14$ underestimates it.
questions.target: Visualizing a Riemann sum approximation
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, right-endpoint rectangles reach up to the curve's height at the RIGHT edge of each strip, so their tops poke above the curve, overestimating the area. Left-endpoint rectangles use the height at the LEFT edge (lower, since $f$ is increasing), so their tops stay below the curve, underestimating the area.

questions.q: For $\int_0^4 x^2\,dx$, the exact value is $\frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$. Rank the four approximations found earlier — $L_4=14$, $R_4=30$, $M_4=21$, $T_4=22$ — from closest to farthest from the exact value, and explain which type of approximation (midpoint or trapezoidal) tends to be more accurate for a smooth curving function.
questions.target: Comparing Riemann sums to the exact integral
questions.cross_lesson: 8.02 Volumes by the Disc and Washer Methods
questions.answer: Distances from $21.33$: $M_4$ ($|21-21.33|=0.33$), $T_4$ ($|22-21.33|=0.67$), $L_4$ ($|14-21.33|=7.33$), $R_4$ ($|30-21.33|=8.67$). Order (closest to farthest): $M_4, T_4, L_4, R_4$. The midpoint approximation tends to be more accurate than the trapezoidal for smooth curves, because its errors are typically about half the size and opposite in sign to the trapezoidal error.

questions.q: For $f(x)=4x^2$ on $[0,5]$, determine whether the Left and Right Riemann Sums overestimate or underestimate $\int_0^{5}f(x)\,dx$.
questions.target: Riemann sums: left, right, and midpoint
choices: Both Left and Right Riemann Sums underestimate.
Both Left and Right Riemann Sums overestimate.
Left Riemann Sum overestimates, and Right Riemann Sum underestimates.
Left Riemann Sum underestimates, and Right Riemann Sum overestimates.
questions.answer: $f(x)=4x^2$ is increasing on $[0,5]$, so left endpoints give smaller values (underestimate) and right endpoints give larger values (overestimate). So: Left Riemann Sum underestimates, and Right Riemann Sum overestimates.
questions.explanation: $f(x)=4x^2$ is increasing on $[0,5]$, so left endpoints give smaller values (underestimate) and right endpoints give larger values (overestimate). So: Left Riemann Sum underestimates, and Right Riemann Sum overestimates.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $[a, b]$, what is the relationship between Left and Right Riemann sums and the true integral value $I$?

choices: Left Sum $< I <$ Right Sum
Right Sum $< I <$ Left Sum
Left Sum $=$ Right Sum

questions.answer: For an increasing function, rectangles using left endpoints underestimate the area while right endpoints overestimate the area: $\mathrm{Left} < I < \mathrm{Right}$.

Trapezoidal Rule underestimates the true value
Trapezoidal Rule is exact

questions.answer: Chords connecting points on a concave up curve lie entirely above the curve, so trapezoids overestimate the true area.

questions.q: Which definite integral is equal to $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n (1 + \frac{2i}{n})^3 \frac{2}{n}$?
questions.target: Limit of a Riemann Sum & Definite Integrals
choices: $\int_1^3 x^3 dx$
$\int_0^2 x^3 dx$
questions.answer: Here $\Delta x = \frac{2}{n}$, interval length $= 2$. $x_i = 1 + i \Delta x \Rightarrow a = 1, b = 3$. The function is $f(x) = x^3$, giving $\int_1^3 x^3 dx$.
questions.explanation: Here $\Delta x = \frac{2}{n}$, interval length $= 2$. $x_i = 1 + i \Delta x \Rightarrow a = 1, b = 3$. The function is $f(x) = x^3$, giving $\int_1^3 x^3 dx$.
